newsitem.title: USA: Gateway 2000 faces uncertain high-end PC demand.
newsitem.headline: Gateway 2000 faces uncertain high-end PC demand.

text.p: Computer direct marketer Gateway 2000 Inc, having warned that its second-quarter revenues will fall short of early projections, is expected to weather a period of disappointing demand for high-end personal computers.
But just how long that period will last is uncertain.

Analysts on Wednesday were split on how long the consumer preference for lower priced equipment will persist. But they agreed that proportionally more sales of lower priced products are hitting industry revenues in general.
New products in the second half of the year, including more digital versatile disk (DVD) products, may increase overall demand for PCs and related equipment, analysts said.
And software providers will catch up with new high-powered chips, such as Intel Corp's MMX and the Pentium 2, potentially boosting demand for computers using those chips.

"I think as new technologies are introduced to increase the functionality of the PC, consumers will want them," said Matthew Russo, an analyst for Sands Brothers & Co. "I don't think people are satiated."
For the time being, however, the cheaper, stripped-down computers or those using original Pentium chips are selling better because of pricing, analysts said.
"They have come out with the $1,500 to $1,600 boxes, which is something they wanted to avoid," said James Poyner, an analyst for Oppenheimer & Co, adding the cheaper products pressure revenues.
"It (Pentium 2) needs to be a hit for this industry or we are going to see categorically a drop in average selling prices," he added.

On Tuesday, Gateway said its second quarter revenues will be flat with the first quarter's $1.42 billion. After announcing first quarter results, Gateway had said it expected revenues to grow slightly in the second quarter versus the first. It reported 1996 second quarter revenues of $1.14 billion.
On Wednesday, Gateway shares traded down 2-7/8 at 31-7/8.
"Over time, most of these large companies ... miss a quarter. But it doesn't mean that they're going to zero," Poyner said.
Gateway said Tuesday that demand was beginning to pick up, but a seasonal spike came later than expected.

The North Sioux City, S.D.-based company also said second quarter operating expenses were running higher than expectations, mainly as a result of investments to support the anticipated strong sales in the second half of the year.

"The analogy of the quarter coming in like a lamb and leaving like a lion appears to hold true this year. It just took longer than expected for the lion to make an appearance," Ted Waitt, Gateway chairman and chief executive, said in a statement Tuesday, adding the outlook for the second half of the year is positive.
Seagate Technology Inc, which makes computer disk drives, on Tuesday issued its second earnings forecast in two weeks and warned of, among other things, weak demand for high-end products.
Micron Technology Inc on Monday reported better-than-expected fiscal third quarter earnings but said falling PC prices and customers' preferences for its low-priced PC products hurt PC gross margins.
